info.bio: La historia de Skinny Puppy comienza en el verano de 1983, cuando Cevin Key (sintetizador y percusiones) y Nivek Ogre (voces) descubren que su atracción por la música extraña y mutante es reciproca y unen sus fuerzas para grabar la maqueta Back & Forth. Este cassette, ahora un tesoro buscado por los fans incondicionales del grupo, llamó la atención de la discográfica "Nettwerk Productions". Asi, Skinny Puppy graban con este sello el E.P. Remission que les permitio salir de las sombras para alcanzar una tímida notoriedad.

scenes.name: Electronic Body Music
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Bélgica acuña una de las corrientes de baile industrial más exitosas, la «electronic body music», derivada del último Cabaret Voltaire con influencia disco y de ciencia ficción: Geography de Front 242 es el disco hito; después Klinik, Neon Judgement, Vomito Negro. En Vancouver, Skinny Puppy y Front Line Assembly, profetas de la generación cyberpunk. Los cimientos de la música de baile alternativa de los noventa.

scenes.name: Industrial, EBM y The Final Cut
scenes.book: Techno Rebels: The Renegades of Electronic Funk
scenes.author: Dan Sicko
scenes.desc: En 1989-1990 quien no escuchaba techno escuchaba industrial: Nitzer Ebb, Skinny Puppy, Front Line Assembly y los belgas Front 242 (Front by Front, 1988), con Chicago como centro americano (Ministry, Die Warzau, My Life with the Thrill Kill Kult, Wax Trax). Detroit tuvo su escena: Code Industry, el único grupo industrial enteramente afroamericano, y The Final Cut, de Jeff Mills y Tony Srock, banda de apoyo del grupo house True Faith (con Bridgett Grace) en Paragon, cuyo productor Jerry Capaldi acabó enfrentado a sus artistas y sembró desconfianza entre techno negro y blanco. Deep into the Cut (1990, Big Sex/Interfisch) cruzó EBM y techno; la última cita de Mills con ellos fue en el festival Atonal de Berlín. Srock los llevó hacia el rock (Consumed, Nettwerk, 1991).

podcast.title: Formation and Unique Sound (1982)
podcast.body: Formed in Vancouver in 1982, Skinny Puppy quickly developed a distinctive sound incorporating keyboards, samplers that used clips from horror movies, drum machines, and loud guitars. The band is considered crucial to the development of the modern industrial sound, perhaps more so than any other early 80s group. "They were formed at Vancouver in 1982 and almost immediately carved out their own special sound with keyboards and samplers that took clips from horror movies. They had drum machines and they had loud guitars."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Use of Found Sounds (1983)
podcast.body: As early as 1983, the Canadian group Skinny Puppy incorporated "found sound" into their music by using bits of dialogue lifted directly from movies to augment their sound. This practice was an early example of using external audio sources to create unique textures and atmospheres. "For example, Canada's skinny puppy used bits of dialogue lifted directly from movies to augment their sound as early as 1983."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dwayne Goettel's Death (August 1995)
podcast.body: Dwayne Goettel, identified as "Duane Gatell" and a member of Skinny Puppy, died in August 1995 from a heroin overdose. "Duane Gatell, skinny puppy, heroin overdose, August 1995."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Breakup and Reunion (1996, 2003)
podcast.body: The band initially broke up in 1996 but reunited in 2003 and has officially remained together ever since. "They did break up in 1996, but they reunited in 2003 and have officially stayed together ever since."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Eight-Year Hiatus and Reunion (2004)
podcast.body: Skinny Puppy was resurrected in 2004 after a period of just over eight years apart. "Skinny Puppy, they were resurrected after a little over eight years in 2004."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 3

podcast.title: Occasional Shows (Post-2013 Album Hiatus)
podcast.body: While there hasn't been a new album since 2013, the band continues to regroup for occasional live performances. "There hasn't been an album since 2013, but they do regroup to play the occasional show that continues today."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lawsuit Against US Military (2014)
podcast.body: Canadian industrial pioneer Skinny Puppy sued the US military in 2014, demanding $666,000 in compensation. The lawsuit was for the unauthorized use of their music on prisoners, a fact the band only discovered after a guard who had served at Guantanamo Bay informed them their songs were being used for "enhanced interrogation." "In 2014, Canadian industrial pioneer Skinny Puppy sued the US military for using their music on prisoners."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Example of Diverse Alternative Music
podcast.body: Skinny Puppy was listed as an example of "heavy industrial music" that was classified as "alternative." This highlights the extensive stylistic diversity that the "alternative" label covered, ranging from industrial sounds to other forms of non-mainstream rock. "Heavy industrial music from skinny pop and ministry was alternative."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Extremely Influential Industrial Band from Vancouver
podcast.body: Skinny Puppy is recognized as an "extremely influential industrial band" originating from Vancouver. "the extremely influential industrial band from Vancouver."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Found by Network Records
podcast.body: Skinny Puppy, a highly non-commercial industrial band that pushed the boundaries of electronic music and the use of samples, was discovered and signed by Network Records. "Network found Skinny Puppy, a highly non-commercial industrial band who pushed the boundaries of electronic music in the use of samples."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 3

podcast.title: Goth and Industrial Blending
podcast.body: Skinny Puppy is noted as a band that straddles the line between Goth and industrial music. "Some bands straddle that line between Goth and industrial just by doing what they do, nine-inch nails and skinny puppy are just two examples."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Heroin Decimation
podcast.body: Heroin tragically decimated and brought death to the band members of Skinny Puppy. "Heroin decimated and brought death to the New York dolls. The pretenders sublime, smashing pumpkins, allyson chains, skinny puppy holes, Scott Wylin, D.D. Ramone, Billy Eidle, a chunk of ever-clear, a vast swath of the Britpop scene of the 1990s, and pretty much everyone who's ever been in the Red Hot Chili Peppers past in present."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Marilyn Manson
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson admired industrial bands like Skinny Puppy. "Cross that with a love for industrial bands like nine-inch nails and skinny puppy"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Other Artists
podcast.body: Their distinctive approach to electronics, heavy beats, and samples had a profound influence on many artists, including Nine Inch Nails and Ministry. "Their approach to electronics and heavy beats and samples influenced everyone from nine inch nails to ministry and beyond."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Trent Reznor
podcast.body: Skinny Puppy was a profound influence on Trent Reznor, particularly their sound's "rage and fury." They were instrumental in his shift away from techno-pop and towards the more aggressive, industrial direction that characterized early Nine Inch Nails material, directly inspiring his first song in this new style, "Down In It." "He found that he really liked the rage and fury of bands like Ministry and Front242 and Canada's Skinny Puppy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Deep Dark Secrets of Nine Inch Nails

podcast.title: Influence on Trent Reznor and Nine Inch Nails
podcast.body: Skinny Puppy's intense and heavy sound, particularly from songs like "Dig It," directly inspired Trent Reznor to re-evaluate his work in techno-pop and subsequently form Nine Inch Nails to emulate their style. "It was songs like that, which made Trent Rezner rethink what he was doing in his Tecno Pop bands, and ultimately he formed 9-inch-dales to emulate Skinny Puppy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Nivek Ogre's Other Bands and Acting Career
podcast.body: The other notable member, Nivek Ogre, has participated in various other bands, including Ministry with Al Jourgensen, and has developed an interest in working on low-budget horror films, with "Queen of Blood" being a mentioned example. "The other member of note is Nivik Ogre. He's been in a bunch of other bands, including Ministry with Al Jorgensen, but he really seems to enjoy working in low budget horror films. You might want to look up a movie called Queen of Blood."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Widespread Influence
podcast.body: Skinny Puppy is cited as a major inspiration and influence for a long list of prominent artists including Ministry, Nine Inch Nails, Marilyn Manson, The Prodigy, Rammstein, Filter, Korn, Linkin Park, and Evanescence. "Here's a short list of artists who say they were inspired and influenced by Skinny Puppy, Ministry, Nine-inch Nails, Maryland Manson, the Prodigy, Ramstein, Filter, Corn, Lincoln Park, Evan Essence."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: cEvin Key's Health and Activism
podcast.body: Member cEvin Key has been involved in multiple musical projects and has publicly battled skin cancer affecting his nose, eye, and lip. In his personal time, he is an active animal rights activist with a particular fondness for cats. "Member Kevin Key has been at the center of a number of different musical projects, but he also battled skin cancer on his nose, eye, and lip. In a spare time, he works as an animal rights activist, and he especially loves cats, apparently."
